cohort: 226 mothers who had undergone cesarean sections and were attending postnatal care services at All ALERT Comprehensive Specialized Hospital.
finding: The prevalence of post-cesarean section wound infections was high (59.29%), with coagulase-negative Staphylococcus and S. aureus being predominant, showing significant resistance to common antibiotics, and was associated with obstructed labor and maternal education level.
mod_finding: Obstructed labor (cephalopelvic disproportion), a common indication for cesarean section, was found to be significantly associated with post-cesarean surgical site infections.
cross-section timing: Data was collected during postnatal care services for mothers who had recently undergone a cesarean section, within the period of December 1, 2020, to May 30, 2021.
